correctness.rationale: For real hexagonal plane N(s,t)=max(|s|,|t|,|s-t|), the defining three-vector quotient is min(N(x+y)^2,N(x-z)^2)/(2N(x)^2+N(y)^2+N(z)^2), with N(y-z)<=a N(x). Universal bound 1 follows by the two triangle inequalities plus (r-s)^2+(r-t)^2>=0. For a>=1 take x=(1,1), y=(0,1), z=(-1,0), yielding both shifted norms 2, denominator 4 and separation 1; strict-constraint endpoint a=1 follows by taking y=(0,1-e), z=(-(1-e),0) and e down to 0. If subcritical a<1 saturated as supremum, normalize a maximizing triple to the compact unit-ball domain; the nonzero limit has r=s=t=1 and N(x+y)=N(x-z)=2. Supporting-face equality forces x and y on one exposed edge and x and -z on one exposed edge. If x is edge-interior, both companion vectors share the same face and N(y-z)>=2; if a vertex, incident same-edge or cross-edge faces force N(y-z)>=1. This contradicts separation <=a<1. Independent exact rational endpoint fractions and finite vertex/edge geometry confirm; the proof, not sampled parameters, handles every a>0.
